# Limitations and Honest Metrics

This document states what is real, what is approximate, and what is
intentionally out of scope. No metrics are invented.

## ML classifier (real trained model)

Trained **from scratch** (compact custom CNN; torchvision is used only for
data loading/augmentation, not pretrained transfer-learning weights) on a
**synthetic** image dataset generated by
`ml-service/training/prepare_dataset.py`. The dataset is procedurally drawn
shapes/textures — it is not real factory photography. An independent
evaluation script (`training/evaluate.py`) reports the test-set accuracy,
per-class accuracy, and a 6×6 confusion matrix.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Model | `defect-classifier` v0.1.0 |
| Classes | OK, SCRATCH, DENT, DISCOLORATION, CRACK, MISALIGNMENT (6) |
| Dataset size | 720 images (504 train / 107 val / 109 test) |
| Training | 30 epochs, CPU, augmentation on the train split only |
| **Test accuracy** | **0.7064 (70.6%)** — deterministic, reproduced by `training/evaluate.py` |
| Per-class test accuracy | OK 0.889, SCRATCH 0.842, DENT 0.947, **DISCOLORATION 0.091**, CRACK 0.667, MISALIGNMENT 1.000 |

Confusion matrix on the 109-image test set (rows = actual, columns =
predicted; class order OK, SCRATCH, DENT, DISCOLORATION, CRACK,
MISALIGNMENT):

| actual \ predicted | OK | SCRATCH | DENT | DISCOLORATION | CRACK | MISALIGNMENT |
|--------------------|----|---------|------|---------------|-------|--------------|
| OK | 16 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| SCRATCH | 2 | 16 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
| DENT | 1 | 0 | 18 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| DISCOLORATION | 20 | 0 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| CRACK | 1 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 12 | 0 |
| MISALIGNMENT | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 13 |

**DISCOLORATION is effectively unlearned (9%):** 20 of its 22 test images are
misclassified as OK, which the pipeline treats as the safe class — the
strongest reason the model is never trusted without human review. The model
is a working demonstration of the full ML pipeline (train → export → serve →
DB-stored results with per-class probabilities), not a production-grade
defect detector. Retraining on real labeled photography with more
epochs/augmentation is the expected next step; `training/` scripts are
generic. Val/test preprocessing is deterministic (resize + normalize only,
matching production inference), so the numbers above are reproducible with
`python training/evaluate.py`.

The backend never trusts the model blindly: every prediction is stored as a
`modelResult` and requires human review confirmation before a defect is
created. The model's OK/POTENTIALLY_DEFECTIVE gating is advisory.

## GenAI assistant

- Default configuration is `GENAI_PROVIDER=none`: responses are deterministic
  database-derived summaries labelled `[DEVELOPMENT MODE - no LLM configured]`,
  with `generated: false` and `mode: dev-no-llm`. These are **not** LLM answers.
- With a real OpenAI-compatible provider configured, answers are grounded in
  retrieved authorized records; cited `DEF-`/`CA-` IDs not present in the
  evidence are replaced with `[unverified-id]` and reported as missing
  evidence. This blocks the classic "invented citation" failure but does not
  guarantee factual correctness of the prose.
- No LLM fine-tuning, no RAG over document corpora, no streaming.

## Backend

- 78 automated tests pass (unit: JWT, idempotency, defect/action state
  machines, GenAI scenarios including misleading-premise and citation
  grounding; integration: RBAC, user admin, registration/OTP, idempotency
  replay, review-queue priority, AI endpoint security against
  `qualityinspect_test`). There is no exhaustive coverage of every edge case.
- Idempotency protects POSTs that opt in via the `Idempotency-Key` header
  (`/inspections`, `/defects`, `/actions`, `/batches/{id}/decisions`);
  clients must send the header to get the protection.
- Refresh tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes with rotation; there is no
  distributed token store (single-node assumption).
- Storage is a local private directory. S3-compatible storage is an interface
  away but not implemented.
- Audit events are append-only at the application layer; the DB user also has
  no UPDATE/DELETE grants on the audit table (defense in depth), but this has
  not been penetration-tested.

## Android app

- Builds to a debug APK (9.0 MB) with all 18 screens implemented. It has not
  been run on a physical device fleet; camera behavior varies by OEM.
- **No offline capture/upload queue.** WorkManager is used only to pre-warm
  the dashboard summary in the background; uploads require connectivity.
- Session tokens are stored in plain app-private `SharedPreferences` (the
  `security-crypto` dependency is declared but not wired in).
- No instrumentation/UI tests (would require an emulator harness).
- The ZXing barcode scanner and gallery image upload have not been
  stress-tested with very large images or galleries.

## Infrastructure / scope

- Single-tenant (`orgId` column exists but no tenant isolation logic).
- No email/SMS notifications, no SSO/OIDC, no rate limiting, no Kubernetes
  manifests (plain `spring-boot:run` / `uvicorn` / `gradle` commands).
- OpenAPI spec covers the API but has not been contract-tested against the
  implementation for every endpoint.
- The demo data path (synthetic images + dev-no-llm GenAI) means an evaluator
  sees labelled development behavior by default — this is deliberate, so the
  system never pretends an LLM or a production model is present when it is not.
